chip.p.name: Project name
chip.p.tools.ph: Empty: the tools on the search path
chip.p.pdk.ph: Where your process design kit is
chip.p.studio: Studio runs the tools you installed yourself, from the tools folder (or the search path), as separate programs. The first run asks you to allow Node to run the add-on's run script.
chip.p.web: This is the browser edition: it reads and shows results, but cannot start programs. Use Flow › Save run package and run it on your computer, or open the project in CadCraft Studio.
chip.p.honest: Nothing is bundled: no simulator, synthesis or layout tool and no PDK comes with CadCraft. For learning and open-silicon flows, not a signed-off tape-out system.
chip.p.memory: This browser does not keep the files after the page closes: save the project.

chip.p.badopen: That is not a Chip design project: {why}

chip.files.binary: A binary file ({kb} KB): not shown as text.
chip.files.badname: {name} is not a file name the project can keep (letters, digits, _ . + - and / only).
chip.flow.studio: Runs in Studio with your own tools.
chip.flow.web: Browser edition: Run needs CadCraft Studio. Save the run package to run it by hand (node engine/cc-chip-run.mjs chip-job.json), then Open a result.
chip.flow.badresult: That is not a result of this add-on: {why}

chip.flow.last.bad: Last run {at} with {tool}: problems, {n} input files.
chip.flow.same: The inputs are the same as then.
chip.opts.sim: testbench (module), defines {NAME: value}, plusargs ["+x=1"]. Icarus adds a small module that dumps every signal to out/wave.vcd; Verilator shows waves only when your testbench calls $dumpfile.
chip.opts.synth: liberty (a .lib file of the project), period (ns), flatten (true/false), exclude [files], script (your own .ys).
chip.opts.pnr: lefs [tech LEF first, then cells], libs [.lib], netlist (e.g. out/synth/netlist.v), sdc, site, utilization, hLayers, vLayers, density, route (global, detailed or none), rcx (extraction rules, for SPEF), script (your own .tcl).
chip.opts.drc: gds (the layout), deck (your PDK's DRC deck), top (cell), vars {input, report, topcell}: the names the deck reads.
chip.opts.lvs: layout (extracted netlist), layoutCell, schematic (netlist), schematicCell, setup (your PDK's Netgen setup file).
chip.opts.gls: netlist, cells [your PDK's cell models], sdf (from place and route), dut (the instance, e.g. counter_tb.dut).
chip.opts.stil: As gate-level simulation (or the RTL design with no netlist), plus period and strobe (in the dump's time units), scope, inputs [], outputs [], clock [names].
chip.sum.pnr: Design area {area} µm², utilization {util} %, worst slack {wns}.
chip.sum.nodef: The layout came back, but the DEF reader is not in this add-on yet.
chip.sum.lvs.ok: Layout and schematic match ({n} cells compared).
chip.sum.lvs.bad: Layout and schematic do not match ({n} cells compared).
chip.sum.waves: The waves are in the Waves tab.
chip.sum.rows: {errors} errors and {warnings} warnings are in Problems.
chip.stil.nowriter: The STIL writer is not in this add-on yet; the {n} vectors were saved as out/stil/patterns.json.
chip.stil.unknown: {n} input values were x or z at their drive time and were written as 0.
chip.wave.none: No .vcd files yet: run a simulation or add one.
chip.wave.cut: Only the first part was read (very large file).
chip.wave.bad: This is not a VCD file this viewer can read.
chip.wave.fst: This is an FST file. FST is not read yet: ask your simulator for VCD (Icarus: $dumpfile("x.vcd"); Verilator: --trace, not --trace-fst).
chip.layout.none: No .def files yet: run place and route or add one.
chip.layout.noreader: The DEF reader is not in this add-on yet.
chip.layout.problems: {n} lines of the DEF were not understood.
chip.layout.counts: {cells} cells, {wires} wire pieces ({unknown} cells with no LEF size).

chip.honest.title: What this is, and what it is not
chip.honest.text: For learning and open-silicon flows, not a signed-off tape-out system. We ship no PDK and make no foundry claims. The tools are yours: you install them, and the add-on runs them as separate programs.
chip.honest.ran: run by us on the sample design
chip.cmd.dialog: The Chip design panel is open in a window of its own (this page has no right panel for add-ons).
